text.p: The European Commission said on Tuesday it had fined German manufacturer Systemform GmbH 100,000 Ecus ($123,000) for operating a distribution system that violated European Union competition rules.

"The Commission found that Systemform operated a distribution system that divided up the European market for its products on national lines and which gave Systemform influence over its distributors' resale prices," it said in a statement.

Systemform, which manufactures machinery for handling large computer printouts, banned its EU distributors from exporting Systemform products outside their assigned national territory, the Commission said.
Some contracts also barred distributors from selling products to firms inside their territory who intended to export the goods, it said.
"In addition, all of the contracts required that resale prices either be set jointly by Systemform and the distributor, or at least that Systemform be kept informed of resale prices."

The Commission said that in deciding the amount of the fine, it had taken into account the fact that Systemform did not dispute its findings and began to amend its contracts before the Commission sent a formal "statement of objections". -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
